findings.title: Strategy enum: Rust renamed C → Reserved at G23-0a but TS union still spells "C"
findings.evidence: crates/benten-ivm/src/strategy.rs:59-84 = `Strategy { A, B, Reserved }`; packages/engine/src/types.ts:1017 = `export type Strategy = "A" | "B" | "C";`; bindings/napi/src/view.rs:139 accepts both `"C"` and `"RESERVED"`.
findings.disposition: DISAGREE-WITH-EXPLANATION (HARD RULE 12(c)) — pre-existing documented wire-stable asymmetry, not drift. The Rust comment at strategy.rs:80-91 explicitly states 'The on-disk wire `ErrorCode` name `E_VIEW_STRATEGY_C_RESERVED` is preserved across the rename for wire stability', and the TS docstring at types.ts:1010-1016 documents the C-as-canonical-wire-name. The napi parser accepts both spellings as backward compat. The asymmetry is by design + documented + tested; flagging would re-litigate a settled wire-stability decision. The TS docstring could be tightened to mention `"C"` is the wire-stable name for what Rust now spells `Reserved` (currently buried in an ErrorCode fixHint), but this is doc-polish, not a §3.5g mirror violation.
